title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Electrical
plain: The computer found an open or shorted circuit in the wiring for the second pressure control solenoid.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)
Sticking valve in the valve body

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
fix: Usually a new pressure control solenoid (on some models part of the solenoid pack or valve body) or a wiring repair; check the fluid first.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Intermittent
plain: The circuit for the second pressure control solenoid is cutting in and out, so shift feel may change from drive to drive.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)
Sticking valve in the valve body

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
fix: Usually a new pressure control solenoid (on some models part of the solenoid pack or valve body) or a wiring repair; check the fluid first.

title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit - Loss of Direction Signal
plain: The output speed sensor on this transmission also reports which way the wheels are turning, and the computer has lost that direction signal.
symptoms: Shifting or hill-hold features may misbehave

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Check the output speed and direction reading on a scanner while moving forward and in reverse
fix: Usually a new output speed sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit - Direction Error
plain: The output speed sensor reports the wheels turning in a direction that doesn't match the gear selected.
symptoms: Shifting or hill-hold features may misbehave

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Check the output speed and direction reading on a scanner while moving forward and in reverse
fix: Usually a new output speed sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Shift Error
plain: The computer commanded a gear change but didn't see the transmission complete it the way it should.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low, burnt or wrong transmission fluid
Sticking valve in the valve body
Worn clutches or bands inside the transmission

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Check for solenoid or speed sensor codes and fix those first
Road test and watch the shift on a scanner
fix: Correct the fluid first, then repair the shift solenoid or valve body; internal wear may need a rebuild.

cost.job: Replace shift solenoid pack or valve body

title: Shift/Timing Solenoid A
plain: There's a problem with shift timing solenoid A, which helps the transmission time its gear changes smoothly.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
fix: Usually a new shift timing solenoid or a wiring repair.

title: Shift/Timing Solenoid A Range/Performance
plain: Shift timing solenoid A isn't responding the way the computer expects, which can make shifts poorly timed.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
fix: Usually a new shift timing solenoid or a wiring repair.

title: Shift/Timing Solenoid A Low
plain: The circuit for shift timing solenoid A reads lower than normal, often from a short to ground.

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
fix: Usually a new shift timing solenoid or a wiring repair.

plain: The circuit for shift timing solenoid A reads higher than normal, often from an open wire or short to power.

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
fix: Usually a new shift timing solenoid or a wiring repair.

title: Normal/Performance Switch Circuit
plain: There's a problem in the circuit for the button that switches the transmission between normal and sport (performance) shifting.
symptoms: Sport or power mode button may not work
Mode light on the dash may not change

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector to the switch
Liquid spilled into the shifter or console

checks: Test whether the button changes the dash indicator
Inspect the switch and its wiring
fix: Usually a new mode switch or a wiring repair.

title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit
plain: The computer isn't getting a good signal from the sensor that measures the speed of a shaft in the middle of the transmission.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor
Metal debris on the sensor tip

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Watch the intermediate speed reading on a scanner while driving
fix: Usually a new intermediate shaft speed sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The intermediate shaft speed signal doesn't match what the computer expects from the other speed sensors.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor
Metal debris on the sensor tip

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Watch the intermediate speed reading on a scanner while driving
fix: Usually a new intermediate shaft speed sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
plain: The computer isn't getting any signal from the intermediate shaft speed sensor.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor
Metal debris on the sensor tip

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Watch the intermediate speed reading on a scanner while driving
fix: Usually a new intermediate shaft speed sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
plain: The intermediate shaft speed signal keeps dropping in and out, often from a loose connector or damaged wire.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor
Metal debris on the sensor tip

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Watch the intermediate speed reading on a scanner while driving
fix: Usually a new intermediate shaft speed sensor or a wiring repair.
